newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- One day after losing the tax rise battle to Chart Pattana, Amnuay Viravan has decided to resign as deputy prime minister and finance minister. Maj-Gen Sornchai Montriwat, Amnuay's secretary, says he has received the resignation letter and will hand it to the prime minister at Government House this morning. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will visit Cambodia on Saturday as scheduled following assurances that he will be in no danger. Forign Ministry's spokesman says Cambodia's Co-Defence Minister Tea Banh has pledged his safety. Chavalit is due to fly into Phnom Penh from Vientiane. (BANGKOK POST)

- Police investigators in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce loan scandal have been informed in writing by the Attorney General's Office that it will not consider the cases because their statute of limitations have expired. According to a source, the office cites Article 39 of the criminal judgement law, which states that public prosecutors' rights to bring cases to court become void when the statue of limitations expires. (THE NATION)

- The central bank should reconsider its plan to force financial institutions to reveal all their non-performing loans, as the disclosures will cripple many companies, says the Bangkok Bank chief. The disclosures will only worsen problems plaguing the financial sector. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Finance Ministry is preparing a tax hike package to raise an additional 24 billion baht from profitable state enterprises and other sectors for fiscal 1998, says permanent secretary for finance. At this stage, several state enterprises are expected to be asked to contribute more profits to the Finance Ministry to help cover the expected revenue shortfall in fiscal 1998 which starts in October. (THE NATION)
